turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos reports 302.9 million pesos invested in water and sanitation this year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette has the numbers ahead of the mayor's second report on 21 November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: OOMSAPAS raised output at the D1 desalination plant.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It moved from 70 litres per second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Now it reaches 130 litres per second. [chuckle] They also added 20 free water trucks and repaired 4,312 leaks.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They spent 78 million pesos from FISAM after ending the private contract.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The D2 plant in Cabo San Lucas stands at 76.58 percent complete.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It will add 250 litres per second once finished, at a cost of 1.78 billion pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias reports that altered stream beds sent 18 tonnes of waste into the sea.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: This followed the 30 October rains and reached beaches in Los Cabos. [pause] The civil engineers' association is urging all three levels of government to invest in storm-water infrastructure.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050 on the topic of Water. Our reporting asks how these infrastructure projects and drainage problems will shape water security in Los Cabos through 2050.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports that Los Cabos has invested 302.9 million pesos in water and sanitation ahead of Mayor Christian Agúndez's second report on 21 November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That figure covers 20 free water trucks delivered so far.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? 20 trucks.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They also installed 39,058 meters during the same period.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is a lot of new meters.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And crews repaired 4,312 leaks.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: After ending the private operator contract, OOMSAPAS spent 78 million pesos from FISAM on the D1 desalination plant.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That money raised output from 70 to 130 litres per second.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The D2 plant in Cabo San Lucas now stands at 76.58 percent completion.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They have already spent 1.78 billion pesos on it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Once finished it should add another 250 litres per second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The city is asking the federal government for 2.1 billion pesos to expand D1 to 200 litres per second.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Sonoreña 2 already has 708 million pesos authorised.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias reports that after the 30 October rains the federal beach-zone office cleared about 18 tonnes of waste from El Médano beach.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They also pulled more than 350 tyres out of the same stretch.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Another 12.5 tonnes of debris came off San José del Cabo beaches.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fifteen washed-away vehicles were removed there too.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Specialists blame altered stream beds that concentrate runoff, and the civil engineers association wants storm-water investment from all three government levels.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México covered Mayor Edith Aguilar's report in Mulegé, where 713 million pesos went into public works over five years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: More than 215 million of that went to water projects.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That work included 23 kilometres of water mains.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They also laid 15 kilometres of new sewers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 240 million pesos went to Guerrero Negro.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Municipal, state and federal governments have begun the first 7 kilometres of the new Palo Verde–Santa Rosalía aqueduct through Conagua.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: She also noted a 70 percent cut in federal works funding for 2026.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A second Meganoticias story says recent rain plus a sewage spill that OOMSAPAS has not fixed for over 20 days are damaging the Transpeni

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The SCT office in BCS confirmed damage mainly on the shoulders between San José and Cabo San Lucas.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The report calls for a full assessment that also addresses the sanitary drainage problem.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep wondering how these separate investments and these spill problems fit together on the same stretch of road.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. One set of numbers shows new capacity, the other shows what happens when drainage stays unresolved.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you ask the water utility first if we could sit down with them?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I would ask how they plan to coordinate the new desalination litres with the storm-water fixes the engineers are requesting.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports that Los Cabos has spent 302.9 million pesos on water and sanitation projects ahead of Mayor Christian Agúndez’s second report on 21 November.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That covers 20 free water trucks, nearly 39,058 meters installed, and over 4,312 leaks fixed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: After the private operator left, OOMSAPAS used 78 million pesos from FISAM to upgrade the D1 desalination plant.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Its output rose from 70 to 130 liters per second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The D2 plant in Cabo San Lucas stands at 76.58 percent complete.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It carries a 1.78 billion peso price tag and will add 250 liters per second once finished.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The city is now asking the federal government for 2.1 billion pesos to push D1 up to 200 liters per second.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Sonoreña 2 already has 708 million pesos authorized. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias adds that 30 October rains sent 18 tonnes of waste and 350 tyres into El Médano beach alone.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Another 12.5 tonnes of debris and 15 vehicles reached San José del Cabo beaches.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Specialists point to altered stream beds that funnel runoff straight to the sea.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The civil engineers’ association calls for coordinated investment in storm-water infrastructure at every government level.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: East Cape sits inside the same growth corridor, where ANP limits and thin infrastructure already shape daily decisions.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That corridor runs from the Cabos all the way to La Paz.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Todos Santos and El Pescadero face aquifer zero three one three in deficit while amenity growth continues.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Residents there still rely on the same municipal systems now being expanded in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The practical question is how quickly the new capacity reaches the Pacific side of the corridor.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Until then, water trucks and leak repairs remain the immediate tools for households and businesses.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same rains that exposed drainage gaps also showed why desalination alone cannot solve every local shortage.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Both municipalities share the Cabos–La Paz focus corridor, so any shortfall in one place quickly affects the other.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you ask the engineers first about those stream beds?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: How soon the three levels of government can actually agree on the funding line.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México reported on 13 November that Los Cabos shut 25 illegal connections this year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That is a lot of taps closed in one place.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The theft was running above 300 litres per second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 300 litres every second adds up fast across a whole town.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Right next to that, Quepoca says the second desalination plant in Cabo San Lucas is already 75 percent complete.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The plant will add 250 litres per second once it is running.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That would bring combined capacity to 655 litres per second for more than 200,000 residents.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the supply side is moving, yet the theft numbers show the old network is still leaking before water reaches the new pipes.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Palabra BCS noted the MXN 48 million paving project on Francisco King Rondero in La Paz.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those works also replace water and sewer lines for 13,000 residents.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The lines go straight to the local utility.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That same utility just asked Conagua for two new Vactor trucks because only two of four are working.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México quoted the utility head saying spills are prioritised for hospitals and tourist zones first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's earlier Foresight editions kept returning to the same line.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Water, grid and places set the 2050 ceiling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The knowledge graph lists four key aquifers in the south already in deficit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Any growth scenario needs new supply or reuse.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias added that between 2021 and 2026 Los Cabos received just MXN 2.02 million in state water-works money.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Out of MXN 401.27m total across the state.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That is the smallest share among the five municipalities.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Even though Los Cabos drives most of the tourism demand.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Tribuna de México reported CEA's overall MXN 400 million across 134 actions.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Including the Palo Verde aqueduct and studies for El Novillo dam.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But the same report shows Los Cabos still waits on the wastewater treatment project.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The governor called it extremely delicate.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Noticabo covered the relocation of the Fonatur plant in San José del Cabo.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It will pump 350 litres per second to La Sonoreña instead of discharging into the estuary.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The governor asked Conagua to speed that project, which is only 60 percent advanced.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Here is the surprising part.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: While the desal plant advances and illegal taps are being cut, the same municipality that needs the water most received the least state investment over five years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Península Digital quoted the governor saying the shortage remains extremely delicate.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The earlier Foresight editions already flagged that without balancing capacity in the CSL–SJD corridor, the housing and tourism numbers cannot keep rising.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the hidden thread is the same pipe network that the paving crews are replacing.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The trucks that cannot keep up, and the new desal capacity still years from full operation.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Every new street and every new plant still runs through that single constraint the portal keeps naming.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The 2050 ceiling starts with how much water actually arrives. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Did you know that 22 of the 39 aquifers in Baja California Sur are in deficit?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: CONAGUA reported the combined shortfall at negative 105.1 cubic hectometers each year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 105.1 is a big gap to close every twelve months.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It shows the underground reserves are being drawn down faster than they refill across most of the state.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Wait, how does that look in daily life for someone in Comondú?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: After storm Polo the protective levee at Puerto San Carlos failed and water supply lines were hit along with roads.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One aquifer listed in the portal data shows a deficit of 24.07.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Another nearby one sits at negative 13.49.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Those numbers come straight from the 2024 availability figures.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: In places where availability is still listed, one site shows roughly 107682 cubic meters remaining.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That amount supports daily use for a limited number of households before it runs lower.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Residents in Cabo San Lucas marched recently to highlight exactly this pressure on supply.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Los Cabos Hotel Association also noted the need for new sources before growth can continue.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meanwhile the state still leads in tourism investment, which makes the water gap more visible each season.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: At the Foro Mar de Cortés Summit Agustín Coppel called for three point five percent annual growth across the region for 20 years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal flags the same tension between regional growth plans and the physical limit of the aquifers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A five state treaty has been suggested to manage the shared Sea of Cortez resources more carefully.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Without coordinated steps the deficit figures are unlikely to improve by 2050.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It leaves every municipality asking the same practical question about how much new development the current water balance can support. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. The data gives a clear starting point for those local decisions.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Portal notes from 30 September 2026 list a dedicated water mesa inside the BCS 2050 work tables.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Who runs that one?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: CEA and CONAGUA lead it, according to the same notes.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Those notes sit inside the larger BCS 2050 database.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That mesa forms part of a larger viability package.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The package tests whether any project still works once water, energy, and land rules all connect.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What exactly gets checked?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Water comes from DMA aquifers or desal plants.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? That couples directly to the energy side.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Energy ties into SIBCS and CFE plans.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Land rules follow POERBCS and the local PDU.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It also flags protected areas and coastal limits.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Four key southern aquifers already sit in DMA deficit. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So any growth without new supply faces a design veto.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos housing capacity stays locked to the PDU plus water and energy limits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tourism in the CSL–SJD corridor drives most of that demand.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: La Paz and the Malecón add lighter pressure on aquifer 0324.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The data still show no planned industrial park with a recorded site or load.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Viability checks for industry must therefore stay inside SIBCS, DMA, and the POER or PDU rules.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: IRENA reported in 2024 that BCS holds top-tier solar resource.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That resource could support lower-cost desal.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Asset management under ISO 55000 guidance from the Institute of Asset Management covers the networks themselves.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: IPCC findings from 2019 add the sea-level constraint for any new intake or outfall.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The ontology simply asks whether the coupled factors still allow the project to proceed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That question stays open until the mesas finish their review.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep wondering how the tables will weigh the missing industrial piece. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's Vision for water opens with the documented constraint: 22 of 39 aquifers sit in deficit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That already signals a tight limit on future options.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: CONAGUA 2023 data puts the total shortfall at −105.1 hm³ per year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. One number like that changes how every growth plan has to be read.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: ENCIG 2025, cited in local coverage, adds that only three in ten people in the state have constant supply.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And 25 illegal taps already recorded in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: With extraction above 300 l/s diverted before it reaches users.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's aspiration is straightforward: new growth not carried by those deficit aquifers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Continuous supply no longer the exception, and reuse counting toward the margin.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: No published 2050 equilibrium target exists in the vision.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The levers listed are already concrete.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One is the second Cabo San Lucas desal plant at 75 percent.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It will add 250 l/s.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: For a combined 655 l/s once finished in 2027.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It is framed as a supply addition, not permission to keep drawing from deficit aquifers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Another lever is closing illegal taps and treating the diverted volume as lost water.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Growth permits should tie directly to mean annual availability per aquifer under NOM-011.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And to sources that do not claim credit against the deficit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal also wants its demand-supply board used so one municipality's deficit is not offset on paper by headroom elsewhere.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The tendencia 2050 reading is a polycentric system rather than one coastal formula repeated from south to north.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos stays the tourism engine under water and power stress; La Paz serves as the service capital and water-energy node.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Comondú keeps its agricultural role with relatively more room; northern Mulegé is the thinly documented corridor with the new remote generation tender.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The conditions require each vocation to keep its distinct role.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: New tourism or residential growth only where water and energy show evidenced margin or a non-DMA source such as desal, without pretending NOM-011 credit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: East Cape and Loreto must respect ANP and POEL ceilings before scaling hospitality.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The watchlist includes Los Cabos POEL 2026 consultation on water and waste obligations, plus the federal bill that sets up to 10 years in prison for water theft.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the second Cabo San Lucas desal plant progress at 75 percent.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep coming back to how the board would actually prevent paper offsets between municipalities.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That is the practical test still ahead. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos has issued reports on its spending for water and sanitation services, while the desalination plants there show clear progress on capacity.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: In Mulegé the new Palo Verde to Santa Rosalía aqueduct has started construction after years of public works funding.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Those steps point to local governments taking direct responsibility for supply lines, though federal money for such projects has dropped sharply.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: At the same time Los Cabos still faces altered stream beds that carry waste straight into the sea and spills that damage the Transpeninsular highway.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Senator Susana Zatarain has put forward a bill that would make water theft a crime carrying prison time, after illegal connections were already found this year in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Wait—how does that change the daily picture for people who rely on the pipes?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The changes mean new infrastructure can reduce pressure on stressed aquifers and support steady supply, yet drainage problems and theft remain open issues that local utilities must still fix.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What stays unclear is exactly how the completed plants and the new aqueduct will shift the overall balance once they are running.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's aspiration describes a future where growth avoids drawing on already short aquifers and reuse becomes a reliable part of the margin, but no official path to that point has been set.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering who will track whether those gaps actually close.
